title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5% above regular)
drivers.evidence: Historical weeks at $10.81 show median sales at 86% of baseline; noise-adjusted price effect is -6%.

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: New competitive threat with no prior data; plausible demand loss based on store proximity and category competition.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 35.0. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 5.5% above regular, which historically correlates with a 6% demand drop (noise-adjusted). A competitor opening across the street introduces a downside risk. Past price hikes above 10.25 (e.g., 10.81) show median sales at 86% of baseline. The 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 weeks at $10.81 saw 49 and 31 units (avg 40 → 1.14x baseline), but no post-event dip suggests no pantry loading. The competitor entry is a new, untested risk, so evidence is thin. Combining a 6% price impact and competitor threat with low confidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 35.0 | 5%-95%: 18.9 - 57.9 | 10%-90%: 21.2 - 54.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
